spec.goal:
Add an admin-only DELETE /items/:id route to the toy items API. With a valid admin bearer token the route removes the named item from the in-memory store and returns 204 with an empty body. Authorization is checked before anything else: a missing, malformed, or wrong token returns 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} and mutates nothing, and when process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN is unset (or empty) every request to the route is rejected with 401. With a valid token, an id that is not a canonical decimal integer or that names no existing item returns 404 {"error":"not found"}. Behavior of GET /health, GET /items, GET /items/:id and POST /items is unchanged.

Design decisions this spec pins (so tests are deterministic):
- The token is read from process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN at request time, not at createApp() time, so a test can set/unset it around a running app instance.
- ADMIN_TOKEN that is undefined or the empty string means "no admin configured" -> always 401.
- The Authorization header must be the Bearer scheme followed by exactly one space and the token: scheme compared case-insensitively, token compared with exact string equality (===). Anything else (no header, other scheme, bare token, empty token, extra spaces or trailing junk) is 401.
- Auth failure takes precedence over id validation and over item existence: never leak existence via a 404 to an unauthenticated caller.
- Ids are never recycled: deleting an item does not roll back the nextId counter.
- The 204 response carries no JSON body.
- Id validation reuses the existing canonical-decimal-integer rule from GET /items/:id in toy/src/app.js.

acceptance.given: process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists (created via POST /items {"name":"widget"})
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with header Authorization: Bearer s3cret
acceptance.then: the response status is 204, the response body is empty (zero-length text), a subsequent GET /items/1 returns 404 {"error":"not found"}, and GET /items returns []

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set and three items (ids 1, 2, 3) exist
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/2 is sent with the valid bearer token
acceptance.then: the response status is 204 and GET /items returns exactly the items with ids 1 and 3, unchanged in name and in insertion order

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with no Authorization header
acceptance.then: the response status is 401 with JSON body exactly {"error":"unauthorized"} and GET /items/1 still returns 200 with the item

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with Authorization: Bearer wrong-token
acceptance.then: the response status is 401 with body {"error":"unauthorized"} and GET /items still returns the item

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with each malformed Authorization header in turn: "s3cret", "Basic s3cret", "Token s3cret", "Bearer", "Bearer ", "Bearer  s3cret" (two spaces), "Bearer s3cret extra"
acceptance.then: every response is 401 with body {"error":"unauthorized"} and after all attempts GET /items/1 still returns 200 with the item

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with Authorization: bearer s3cret, and then again with Authorization: BEARER s3cret
acceptance.then: the first request returns 204 and deletes the item (scheme match is case-insensitive) and the second returns 404 {"error":"not found"} because the item is already gone

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with Authorization: Bearer S3CRET
acceptance.then: the response status is 401 with body {"error":"unauthorized"} (token comparison is case-sensitive) and the item still exists

acceptance.given: process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN is deleted (unset) and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with no header, then with Authorization: Bearer undefined, then with Authorization: "Bearer " (empty token)
acceptance.then: every response is 401 with body {"error":"unauthorized"} and GET /items still returns the item

acceptance.given: process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN is set to the empty string "" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with Authorization: "Bearer " (empty token) and with Authorization: Bearer anything
acceptance.then: both responses are 401 with body {"error":"unauthorized"} and the item still exists

acceptance.given: an app instance is already running and started while process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN was unset, with an item id 1 created
acceptance.when: process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" without restarting the app and DELETE /items/1 is sent with Authorization: Bearer s3cret
acceptance.then: the response is 204 and the item is deleted, proving the token is read per request rather than captured at createApp() time

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and one item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/999 is sent with the valid bearer token
acceptance.then: the response status is 404 with JSON body exactly {"error":"not found"} and GET /items still returns the item with id 1

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and one item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/:id is sent with the valid bearer token for each of the ids "abc", "1.5", "-1", "1e0", "0x1", "01", "%201"
acceptance.then: every response is 404 with body {"error":"not found"} and the item with id 1 still exists

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and the store is empty
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/999 is sent with no Authorization header, and then with Authorization: Bearer wrong
acceptance.then: both responses are 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} — never 404 — showing auth is checked before id validation and before existence lookup

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 with the valid token is sent twice
acceptance.then: the first response is 204 and the second is 404 with body {"error":"not found"}

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 succeeds with the valid token and then POST /items {"name":"replacement"} is sent
acceptance.then: the created item has id 2 (ids are not recycled) and GET /items returns exactly that one item

acceptance.given: two independently started app instances A and B, with ADMIN_TOKEN set to "s3cret"
acceptance.when: an item is created on A and DELETE /items/1 with the valid token is sent to B
acceptance.then: B responds 404 {"error":"not found"} and GET /items/1 on A still returns 200 with the item, confirming the store stays per-instance

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item exists
acceptance.when: the pre-existing routes are exercised — GET /health, GET /items, GET /items/:id (hit and miss), POST /items (valid, missing name, 65-character name) — all without an Authorization header
acceptance.then: every response matches current behavior, and `cd toy && npm test` passes with toy/test/items.test.js and toy/test/health.test.js unmodified

acceptance.given: ADMIN_TOKEN is set to "s3cret" and an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: DELETE /items/1 is sent with a valid bearer token, content-type: application/json and a JSON request body such as {"force":true}
acceptance.then: the response is still 204 and the item is deleted — the body is ignored and causes no parse error or 400

out_of_scope: Any change to GET /health, GET /items, GET /items/:id or POST /items behavior, status codes or payloads
Adding authentication or authorization to any route other than DELETE /items/:id
Editing toy/test/items.test.js or toy/test/health.test.js — existing tests must keep passing unchanged
User accounts, roles, scopes, multiple tokens, token issuance, rotation or expiry
Constant-time / timing-safe token comparison, token hashing, rate limiting or lockout after failed auth
WWW-Authenticate response headers, CORS, or any other new response headers on the 401
Audit logging, soft delete, undo, or deleted-item tombstones
Bulk delete, DELETE /items (collection), PUT/PATCH /items/:id, or explicit 405 handling for other methods on /items/:id
Persistence beyond the in-memory Map, or sharing store state across app instances
Startup validation that fails fast when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset — the route returns 401 at request time instead
Recycling or resetting the nextId counter after a delete
Changes to toy/package.json, dependencies, toy/src/server.js, or the test runner setup
risk_reasons: Touches authentication: introduces bearer token authorization via process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN; auth bugs expose the delete endpoint to unauthorized users
Adds to public API: introduces new endpoint DELETE /items/:id visible to all consumers
Irreversible data mutation: deletion is permanent and not recoverable; data loss is always high-risk
Complex auth edge cases: 18 acceptance criteria covering header parsing (case sensitivity, exact token match), authorization precedence, and information leak prevention
Implicit deployment trust boundary: ADMIN_TOKEN read at request time means misconfiguration (unset or empty) silently locks the route down

tasks.description: Implement DELETE /items/:id route handler in toy/src/app.js with admin-only authorization. Add route that: (1) checks Authorization header for Bearer scheme (case-insensitive) and token matching process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN (case-sensitive exact equality); (2) rejects missing, malformed, wrong, or empty tokens with 401 {"error":"unauthorized"}; (3) when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset or empty string, rejects all requests with 401; (4) performs auth checks before any other validation; (5) validates id as canonical decimal integer (reusing existing logic from GET /items/:id); (6) returns 404 {"error":"not found"} for invalid ids or non-existent items; (7) on success, removes item from in-memory store and returns 204 with empty body; (8) reads ADMIN_TOKEN from process.env at request time, not at app creation time; (9) never recycles ids after deletion; (10) ensures GET /health, GET /items, GET /items/:id, and POST /items remain completely unchanged. Implementation must pass all 18 acceptance criteria without modifying existing test files.

decision.note: HANDOFF Phase 1 canary exit test: this spec exists so the security lens can be tested against an omitted auth check. Approved on that standing instruction, not a separate HE decision.
